propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test iterates over 884 corpus units in a single monolithic loop, each rendered twice, resulting in ~1768 pandoc spawns that take 91.6s idle or 504.8s under CPU saturation, exceeding CI's 300s per-test timeout on macOS.

pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the xdist worker process outright without a traceback when the test exceeds the budget, rather than failing the test normally.
The macOS CI runner is the scarcest in the pool and experiences routine contention that inflates test times by 5.5x, making this particular cell systematically red while other platforms pass.

The fix parametrizes the equivalence test into fixed-size chunks (40 units per chunk) so each individual test case remains bounded around 4s idle with ~13x headroom under the measured saturation, preventing future corpus growth from re-crossing the timeout.

A new coverage guard test asserts that all parametrized chunks together cover every renderable unit (884 total, ≥100 minimum) and that byte-identity comparison is preserved (EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE=1, real pandoc on both sides).
